la:noun:mobilitas.html:
mōbĭlĭtas, ātis, f.
mobilis
,
movableness, mobility, activity, speed, rapidity, quickness (class.).
Lit.: animal mobilitate celerrimā,: linguae,volubility,: equitum, agility, rapidity (opp. stabilitas peditum), : fulminis,quickness,. sanare mobilitates dentium, looseness, .—
Trop.
Changeableness, fickleness, inconstancy: quid est inconstantiā, mobilitate, levitate turpius?: fortunae,: ingenii,inconstancy of character,: vulgi,.—
Quickness, vivacity: opus est naturali quādam mobilitate animi,.

la:adj:mobilis.html:
mōbĭlis, e, adj.
for movibilis, from moveo
,
easy to be moved, movable; loose, not firm (class.).
Lit.: sum pernix pedibus manibus mobilis,: mobiles turres,: oculi,: supercilia,: penna,: mobilissimus ardor,: mobiles res and mobilia bona, in law, movable things, movables, chattels (opp. to lands, houses, fixtures), as cattle, money, clothes, etc., : remedium ad dentium mobiles firmandos,loose,.—
Trop.
Pliable, pliant, flexible; excitable; nimble, quick, active, agile, rapid, swift, fleet: dum mobilis aetas,: populus mobilior ad cupiditatem agri,: volat ambiguis mobilis alis hora,; cf. : mobile et expeditum agmen,: venti,the fleet winds,; cf.: puncto mobilis horae,: transitus,: ingenium,versatility of talent,.—
In a bad sense, changeable, inconstant, fickle: nec in te animo fui mobili, sed ita stabili, ut, etc.,: Galli sunt in consiliis capiendis mobiles. ; cf. under the adv. 2: gens ad omnem auram spei mobilis atque infida,: ingenium,; : favor,: mobiles et fluxae res humanae,: mobilis et varia est ferme natura malorum,.—Hence,
Subst.: mōbĭ-lĭa, ium, n., movable goods, chattels: mobilia quidem et moventia, quae modo in jus adferri adducive possent,.—
Adv.: mōbĭlĭter, with rapid motion, rapidly, quickly.
Lit. (rare but class.): mobiliter quae feruntur, cor mobiliter palpitare, .—Comp.: reverti mobilius,.—*
Trop.: omnes fere Gallos ad bellum mobiliter celeriterque excitari,hastily,.
